When it was time to get paid, the boss told his manager to pay the guys hired at 5:00 PM first. He gave them a full day's wage. When the guys who had been sweating in the sun since 6:00 AM stepped up, they expected a massive bonus. But the boss gave them the exact same full-day's wage they had agreed on. The early crew was furious. "This is completely unfair! We worked twelve hours in the blistering heat, and you paid those lazy guys the same amount!" The boss replied, "Friend, I didn't cheat you. We agreed on a price, and I paid it. Take your money and go. Can't I be generous with my own money? Are you jealous because I'm kind?" Jesus summed it up: "The last will be first, and the first will be last."

A Mom's Ambitious Request As they got closer to Jerusalem, the mother of James and John (two of the disciples) came up to Jesus and kneeled down. "When you become King, promise me that my two boys can be your right-hand and left-hand men." Jesus looked at the brothers. "You have no idea what you're asking. Can you drink from the cup of suffering I'm about to drink from?" They confidently said, "We can handle it." Jesus said, "You will suffer like me, but I don't assign the honored seats. My Father does."
When the other ten disciples heard about this, they were absolutely furious at James and John for trying to bypass them for the best jobs. Jesus called a team meeting to shut it down:

"You guys know how the Romans do leadership—they boss people around, flex their power, and make everyone serve them. It is not going to be like that with you. > Whoever wants to be a leader among you must be your servant. Whoever wants to be first must be your slave. I, the Son of Man, didn't come here to be served by you. I came to serve you, and to give my life to buy freedom for many."

As they were leaving Jericho, a huge crowd followed. Two blind men were sitting by the side of the road, and when they heard Jesus was passing by, they shouted, "Master, Son of David, have mercy on us!" The crowd told them to shut up, but they yelled even louder. Jesus stopped and asked, "What do you want Me to do for you?" They said, "Master, we want to see!" Jesus was deeply moved, touched their eyes — and instantly they could see. They got up and joined the crowd following Him.

title: Jesus Makes A Scene
paragraphs: As Jesus and his crew got close to Jerusalem, he sent two disciples on a mission. 'Go into that village,' he said, 'and you'll find a donkey and her colt. Untie them and bring them to me. If anyone gives you a hard time, just say, ‘The Master needs them,’ and they’ll let you go.' So they did it, and Jesus rode into town on the donkey. The crowd went absolutely wild, throwing their jackets on the ground like a red carpet and waving palm branches. They were all screaming, 'Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in God's name!'

The whole city was buzzing, like, 'Who IS this guy?' The crowd with Jesus was shouting, 'This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth!' Then Jesus went straight to the Temple and lost it. He started flipping tables of the loan sharks and kicking over the stalls of people selling pigeons. He went beast mode, quoting the scriptures: > My house was designated a house of prayer; You have made it a hangout for thieves. After he cleared them out, the blind and the crippled came to him and he healed them right there.

The religious leaders were fuming when they saw all the incredible things he was doing. But what really set them off were the kids running around the Temple shouting, 'Hosanna to the Son of David!' They confronted Jesus, all heated. 'Do you hear what these kids are saying?' Jesus just looked at them and said, 'Yeah, I hear them. Haven't you ever read the scripture that says, ‘From the mouths of children and babies I’ll furnish a place of praise’?'. Mic drop. He was so over their drama that he just turned and walked out of the city to spend the night in Bethany.

The next morning, Jesus was walking back to the city and feeling hungry. He saw a fig tree by the road and went to get some breakfast, but it only had leaves. So he said to the tree, 'No more figs from you—ever!' And right then, the tree withered up into a dry stick. His disciples saw it and their jaws dropped. 'How did that tree just die on the spot?' they asked. Jesus told them, 'Seriously, if you have faith and don’t doubt, you can do more than this. You could tell this mountain, ‘Go jump in the lake,’ and it would. If you believe, you will receive whatever you ask for in prayer.'

Back in the Temple, the high priests and elders cornered him while he was teaching. 'Show us your credentials,' they demanded. 'Who gave you the authority to do all this?' Jesus shot back, 'I'll answer you, but first, you answer me. John the Baptist’s baptism—was it from heaven or from humans?' They were totally stuck. They huddled up, whispering, 'If we say ‘from heaven,’ he’ll ask why we didn’t believe John. If we say ‘from humans,’ the crowd will riot because they all think John was a prophet.' So they came back and said, 'We don’t know.' Jesus replied, 'Then I’m not telling you who gave me my authority either.'

Then Jesus dropped a story on them. 'A man had two sons. He told the first, ‘Go work in the vineyard today.’ The son said, ‘I don’t want to,’ but later he changed his mind and went. The father told the second son the same thing, and he said, ‘Yes, sir!’ but he never went. Which one did what the father wanted?' They answered, 'The first one.' Jesus looked them dead in the eye and said, 'Well, I’m telling you, the tax collectors and immoral women are getting into God’s kingdom ahead of you. John the Baptist came and showed you the right way to live, and you dissed him, but they believed him. Even after seeing their lives change, you still didn’t change your minds and believe.'

He wasn't done yet. 'Listen to this. A landowner planted a vineyard, built a wall around it, and rented it to some farmers before going on a trip. When it was harvest time, he sent his servants to collect his share. But the farmers beat one up, killed another, and stoned a third. He sent more servants, and they did the same thing. Finally, he sent his son, thinking, ‘They’ll respect my son.’ But when the farmers saw the son, they said, ‘This is the heir! Let’s kill him and take his inheritance!' So they grabbed him, threw him out of the vineyard, and murdered him.'

Jesus paused and asked the leaders, 'So when the owner of the vineyard comes back, what will he do to those farmers?' They replied, 'He’ll bring those wretches to a wretched end, and he’ll rent the vineyard to other farmers who will give him his share at harvest time.' Jesus said, 'Exactly. And you've read the scripture: > The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. This is the Lord’s doing, and it is marvelous in our eyes. Therefore I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a people who will produce its fruit.' When the religious leaders heard his stories, they knew he was talking about them. They wanted to arrest him, but they were scared of the crowd, who all thought Jesus was a prophet.

title: Party Crashers & Gotcha Questions
paragraphs: Jesus dropped another parable on them. He said, "God's kingdom is like a king who planned this epic wedding for his son. He sent out the invites to all his guests, but they completely ignored him. Can you believe it? They just wouldn't come!"

The king tried again, sending more servants saying, 'Look, the party is ready to go, the food is amazing, everything is set! Just come!' But the guests couldn't be bothered. One went off to his farm, another to his business. The rest of them actually attacked the servants, beat them up, and killed them. The king absolutely lost it, went beast mode, and sent his army to destroy those murderers and burn their city down.

Then he told his crew, 'The wedding banquet is ready, but the people I invited were a total flop. So go out to the main streets and invite anyone and everyone you find.' The servants went out and gathered a huge crowd of anyone they could find, good and bad, and the wedding hall was finally packed. But when the king came in, he spotted one guy who wasn't wearing the right clothes for the wedding. He asked him, 'Friend, how did you get in here without the proper attire?' The guy had nothing to say. So the king ordered, 'Tie him up and throw him out into the darkness.' Jesus finished with this mic drop: 'Many are invited, but few are chosen.'

The religious leaders were seriously trying to trip Jesus up. They sent their followers along with some government loyalists to trap him. They started by buttering him up, 'Teacher, we know you're legit and teach the way of God, seriously. You don't care about what people think. So tell us, is it right to pay taxes to Caesar or not?' Jesus knew they were being shady and called them out. 'Why are you testing me? Show me the coin used for the tax.'

They handed him a coin, and he asked, 'Whose face and name is on this?' They replied, 'Caesar's.' Jesus then delivered the knockout punch: > "So give back to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's." They were completely stunned and had no comeback. They just left, totally speechless.

Later, some Sadducees, a group who didn't even believe in life after death, came to Jesus with a wild hypothetical. 'Teacher, Moses said if a man dies without kids, his brother should marry the widow. So, here's the story: there were seven brothers. The first one died, then the second, and so on, all seven marrying the same woman. Finally, the woman died. So, at the resurrection, whose wife is she gonna be?'

Jesus told them, "You're way off because you don't know the Scriptures or the power of God. When people rise from the dead, it's not going to be like a royal banquet. People won't be getting married. They will be like the angels in heaven. And about the resurrection, haven't you read what God said to you? He said, 'I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.' He is the God of the living, not the dead." The crowd was blown away by his teaching.

When the Pharisees heard how Jesus had shut down the Sadducees, they regrouped for another attack. One of them, a legal expert, asked him a question to test him: 'Teacher, which is the greatest commandment in the Law?' Jesus replied, > "‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.’ This is the first and greatest commandment. And the second is like it: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’ All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments."

Then Jesus flipped it on the Pharisees with His own question: "What do you think about the Messiah? Whose son is He?" "David's son," they said. Jesus replied, "Then explain this: how come David, speaking by the Spirit, calls the Messiah his \"Master\"? God said to my Master, \"Sit here at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.\" If David calls Him \"Master,\" how can He be his son?" That completely stumped them — and from that day on, nobody dared ask Him any more trap questions.

title: Jesus Calls Out on the Hypocrites
paragraphs: Jesus gathered his crew and the huge crowd and dropped a bomb. He called out the religious leaders, the so-called experts in God's Law. 'Listen, these guys know the rules, but they don't play by 'em. They talk a good game, but their lives are a total mess. It's all for show, like a perpetual parade. They love the honored seats at banquets and getting called 'Doctor' or 'Reverend.' Don't be like them. They're fakes.

Then Jesus flipped the script. He told his followers to ditch the obsession with status and titles. 'Don't let people put you on a pedestal. You have one Teacher, and you're all just classmates.' He made it clear that the only one who deserves that kind of authority is God. The ultimate flex? Being humble. > 'Do you want to stand out? Then step down. Be a servant. If you puff yourself up, you’ll get the wind knocked out of you. But if you’re content to simply be yourself, your life will count for plenty.'

Jesus went full beast mode, calling the religious leaders 'frauds' and 'roadblocks to God's kingdom.' He was like, 'You won't enter, and you won't let anyone else in either!' He called them out for their ridiculous, nit-picky rules. They cared more about tithing every last penny than about actual important things like fairness, compassion, and being committed to God. He said they looked silly, focusing on commas while their whole life story was a fail.

"You're hopeless, you religious scholars and Pharisees — frauds! You travel halfway around the world to win one convert, and then you turn him into someone twice as messed up as you are. You're hopeless! What arrogant stupidity! You say, \"If someone swears with their fingers crossed, it doesn't count — but if they swear with their hand on the Bible, that's serious.\" Seriously? Does the leather on the Bible matter more than the person making the promise? What ridiculous nit-picking! A promise is a promise — God is watching and holding you to it, no matter where you make it or what you swear on."

He kept going, comparing them to cups that are sparkling clean on the outside but are full of rotten, maggoty greed on the inside. 'Foolish Pharisees! Scour the insides, and then the gleaming surface will mean something.' Then he hit them with another one: 'You're like a perfectly manicured graveyard. Looks beautiful with fresh-cut grass and bright flowers, but underneath it's all rotting bones and worm-eaten flesh. You look like saints, but you're total frauds underneath.'

Jesus didn't hold back. He called them 'snakes' and 'cold-blooded sneaks.' He accused them of being just like their ancestors who murdered the prophets. They build fancy tombs for the prophets now, but they're cut from the same cloth. He promised that he would keep sending wise people and prophets, and they would keep treating them like dirt. The guilt for every drop of innocent blood spilled, from Abel to the prophet Zechariah, was going to land right on their heads.

Finally, Jesus looked out over the city and his heart broke. 'Jerusalem! Jerusalem! You murder the prophets and kill the messengers God sends you! How many times have I wanted to gather you up, like a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you wouldn't let me.' His voice was filled with pain. 'Now your city is a ghost town. I'm out of here. You won't see me again until you're ready to say, ‘God has blessed him! He’s come, bringing God’s rule!’'

title: The Real Tea on the End Times
paragraphs: As Jesus and his crew were leaving the Temple, his disciples were totally geeking out over the amazing architecture. 'Hey, Jesus, check out these buildings! So epic!' Jesus just shook his head. 'You think this is impressive? Seriously, every single one of these stones is going to end up in a pile of rubble.' Later, they were chilling on the Mount of Olives, and the disciples cornered him. 'Okay, spill. When is all this going down? And give us a sign so we know when you're coming back and the world as we know it is over.'

Jesus got real serious. 'First thing: Don't get played. A bunch of fakes are gonna show up claiming to be me, the Messiah, and they're gonna fool a lot of people. You'll hear about wars, and rumors of more wars, but don't panic. That's just normal, messed-up history. It's not the end. Countries will throw down with other countries, there will be famines and earthquakes. That's just the warm-up act.'

'Then things get personal. They're gonna turn on you, hate you, and even kill you just because you're on my team. It's going to be brutal, a total dog-eat-dog world where everyone betrays each other. Lying preachers will be everywhere, and the world will get so evil that most people's love will just turn to ash. But you gotta hang in there. The one who stays loyal to the end, that's the one who is saved. And through all the chaos, the good news about God's kingdom will be preached everywhere on the planet. Then the end will come.'

'So, when you see the 'Monster of Desecration' that the prophet Daniel wrote about standing in the holy Temple—you'll know what I'm talking about—it's time to bounce. If you're in Judea, run for the hills. Don't even go back in the house to grab your cloak. It's going to be an awful time, worse than anything the world has ever seen. It'll be so bad that if God didn't cut it short, no one would survive. But for the sake of his chosen ones, he'll hit the brakes on the chaos.'

'During that time, if someone says, 'Quick, the Messiah is over here!' or 'There he is!'—don't buy it. These fake Messiahs and scam-artist preachers will be putting on a big show, doing crazy signs and wonders to trick even the smartest people. I'm giving you the heads-up now so you don't fall for it. My return isn't some secret event you have to RSVP to. It will be like a flash of lightning that lights up the whole sky. Everyone will see it.'

'Right after that terrible time, the universe is gonna go haywire. The sun will go dark, the moon will refuse to shine, stars will fall out of the sky, and all the cosmic powers will be shaken. Then, finally, the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky. Everyone on earth who isn't ready will totally lose it, crying and mourning as they see me arrive on the clouds with insane power and glory. I'll send out my angels with a massive trumpet blast, and they'll gather all my chosen people from every corner of the globe.'

'Learn from the fig tree. As soon as its branches get tender and it starts growing leaves, you know summer is coming. In the same way, when you see all these things happening, you'll know my arrival is right at the door. I'm telling you, this generation won't pass away until all this stuff starts to happen. Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words are forever.'

'But nobody knows the exact day or hour. Not the angels, not even me. Only the Father knows. My arrival will be like the days of Noah. People were just living their lives—eating, drinking, getting married—right up until the day Noah got on the ark. They had no clue what was coming until the flood hit and swept them all away. That's how it will be when I return. So you have to stay ready. You have no idea when your Master is showing up. Be vigilant, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour you don't expect.'

"Who's the kind of servant a master can actually trust with the kitchen — someone who feeds the workers on time, every day, even when the master drops in unannounced? That person is blessed, and the master will put them in charge of the whole operation. But if that servant thinks, \"My master's taking forever,\" and starts beating the other workers and partying it up — the master will show up when they least expect it and throw them out into the cold, dark place where there's nothing but crying and regret."

title: Stay Ready or Get Left Behind
paragraphs: Jesus dropped another parable. He said, ‘God's Kingdom is like ten bridesmaids waiting for the groom to show up for the wedding party. Five of them were totally clueless and the other five were on top of their game. The clueless ones brought their lamps but forgot to bring extra oil, like showing up to a journey with no extra supplies. The smart ones? They brought a whole backup supply.

The groom was running late, so all the girls ended up crashing for a nap. Then, in the middle of the night, someone screamed, 'He's here! The groom is finally here! Let's go!' All ten of them jumped up and got their lamps ready. But the five unprepared girls started to panic. 'Our lamps are dying! Quick, give us some of your oil!'

The smart girls said, 'Sorry, no can do. There isn't enough for all of us. You'll have to run to the store and buy your own.' So they left to go buy more, but while they were gone, the groom arrived. The girls who were ready went into the wedding feast with him, and the door was locked. A little while later, the clueless crew finally showed up, banging on the door. 'Master, let us in!' But he just said, 'Do I even know you? I don't think so.' Then Jesus looked at his crew and said, 'So for real, stay alert. You have no idea when the time will come.'

Then Jesus hit them with another story. 'It's like a boss who was going on a long trip. He called in his top three employees and gave them some major cash to manage. To one, he gave $5,000, to another $2,000, and to the last one $1,000—all based on what he knew they could handle. The first guy immediately went out and hustled, doubling the investment. The second guy did the same. But the third guy, the one with the $1,000, just dug a hole and buried it. He played it way too safe.'

After a super long time, the boss came back to see what was up. The guy with the $5,000 showed him the $10,000 he made. The boss was thrilled! 'Let's go! You killed it! You're not just my employee anymore, you're my partner.' The guy with the $2,000 showed him his $4,000, and the boss said the exact same thing. But then the third guy came up and said, 'Look, I know you're a tough boss and you don't mess around. I was scared I'd mess up and lose your money, so I just hid it. Here's your $1,000 back, safe and sound.'

The boss absolutely lost it. 'You're a terrible employee! It's criminal to be that cautious! If you knew I was serious about results, why did you do the absolute least? You could have at least put it in a savings account and gotten some interest!' Then he told his other guys, 'Take his $1,000 and give it to the one who made the most. And throw this play-it-safe guy out. He's getting kicked out of the company for good.'

Jesus wasn't done. He dropped a bomb. 'When the Son of Man comes back in all his glory with his angel squad, he's going to sit on his throne and judge everyone. All the nations will be lined up, and he'll separate people like a farmer separates sheep from goats. The sheep will be on his right, and the goats on his left.'

Then the King will turn to the sheep on his right and say, 'Come on in, you're blessed by my Father! Your spot in the kingdom has been ready since day one. Why? Because when I was hungry, you fed me. When I was thirsty, you gave me a drink. When I was a stranger, you took me in. When I was freezing, you gave me clothes. When I was sick, you checked on me. When I was in jail, you visited me.'

The sheep will be totally confused. 'Wait, what? When did we ever see you hungry or thirsty or in jail?' And the King will say, > 'I'm telling you the honest truth: whenever you did one of these things for the least important person, you were doing it for me.'

Then he'll turn to the goats on his left and go beast mode. 'Get out of here, you useless goats! You're headed for eternal fire. Why? Because I was hungry, and you didn't give me any food. I was thirsty, and you gave me nothing to drink. I was a stranger, and you ignored me. I was freezing, and you didn't offer a coat. I was sick and in jail, and you never even thought to visit.' They'll argue back, 'Master, when did we ever see you in need and not help?' And he'll reply, 'Seriously, whenever you failed to help someone who was overlooked, you were failing to help me.' And those goats will be sent to their eternal punishment, but the sheep will enter eternal life.

title: The Final Hours
paragraphs: Jesus dropped a bomb on his disciples, saying, 'You know Passover is in two days? That's when I get betrayed and crucified.' At the same time, the religious leaders were plotting to arrest and kill him on the down-low, because they were scared of a riot if they did it publicly.

While Jesus was having dinner at Simon the Leper's house, a woman came in and did something totally extra. She poured a whole bottle of super expensive perfume on his head. The disciples lost it, saying, 'What a waste! That could have been sold and the money given to the poor!' But Jesus shut them down, saying, 'Why are you giving her a hard time? She did a beautiful thing for me. You'll always have the poor with you, but you won't always have me. She was preparing me for my burial. I promise you, wherever the good news is preached, what she has done will be told in memory of her.'

That's when Judas, one of the twelve, went full-on snake. He went to the chief priests and asked, 'What will you give me if I hand him over to you?' They offered him thirty pieces of silver, and from then on, he was looking for the right moment to betray Jesus.

At the Last Supper, things got real. Jesus told them, 'One of you is going to betray me.' The disciples were stunned, each one asking, 'It's not me, is it?' Jesus explained it was the one who dipped his bread in the bowl with him. Then Judas, playing innocent, asked, 'It's not me, is it, Rabbi?' Jesus just said, 'You said it.'

During the meal, Jesus took some bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to his disciples. > Take, eat. This is my body. Then he took a cup of wine, thanked God for it, and said, > Drink this, all of you. This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.

"I'm telling you, I won't drink wine again until the day I drink it with you in My Father's kingdom." Then they sang a hymn and headed out to the Mount of Olives. On the way, Jesus told them, "Tonight, every one of you is going to bail on Me. There's a Scripture that says, \"I'll strike the shepherd, and the sheep will scatter.\" But after I'm raised back to life, I'll go ahead of you to Galilee." Peter shot back, "Even if everyone else bails, I never will!" Jesus said, "I'm telling you the truth — tonight, before the rooster crows, you're going to deny Me three times." Peter insisted, "Even if I have to die with You, I'll never deny You!" And all the other disciples said the exact same thing.

Later, in the garden of Gethsemane, Jesus was in agony, praying, 'My Father, if it is possible, may this cup be taken from me. Yet not as I will, but as you will.' He found his disciples sleeping and said to Peter, 'Couldn't you keep watch with me for one hour?' He prayed two more times, each time finding them asleep. The last time, he said, 'Are you still sleeping? Look, the hour is near, and the Son of Man is delivered into the hands of sinners. Rise, let us go. Here comes my betrayer.'

Right on cue, Judas showed up with a mob armed with swords and clubs. He had told them, 'The one I kiss is the man; arrest him.' He went up to Jesus, said, 'Greetings, Rabbi!' and kissed him. As the mob grabbed Jesus, Peter went beast mode, pulled out a sword, and sliced off a servant's ear. But Jesus told him to put it away, saying, 'Do you think I cannot call on my Father, and he will at once put at my disposal more than twelve legions of angels?' Then all the disciples bailed.

They took Jesus to the high priest, Caiaphas, for a sham trial. They brought in a bunch of liars to testify against him, but their stories were all over the place. Finally, two came forward and said, 'This fellow said, 'I am able to destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days.'' The high priest stood up and asked Jesus, 'Have you no answer?' But Jesus stayed silent. So the high priest said, 'I charge you under oath by the living God: Tell us if you are the Messiah, the Son of God.' Jesus replied, 'You have said so. But I say to all of you: From now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the Mighty One and coming on the clouds of heaven.' The high priest lost it, tore his clothes, and yelled, 'Blasphemy!' The whole council condemned him to death and then they started spitting on him and beating him.

Meanwhile, Peter was outside in the courtyard, and a servant girl came up to him and said, 'You also were with Jesus of Galilee.' But he denied it, saying, 'I don't know what you're talking about.' He went out to the gateway, where another girl saw him and said, 'This fellow was with Jesus of Nazareth.' He denied it again, with an oath: 'I don't know the man!' A little later, the bystanders said to Peter, 'Surely you are one of them; your accent gives you away.' Then he began to call down curses, and he swore to them, 'I don't know the man!' Immediately a rooster crowed, and Peter remembered what Jesus had said: 'Before the rooster crows, you will disown me three times.' And he went outside and wept bitterly.

title: The King They Crucified
paragraphs: As soon as the sun was up, the religious leaders put the final touches on their shady plan to execute Jesus. They tied him up and hauled him off to the governor, Pilate, like a criminal.

When Judas, the friend who betrayed him, saw that Jesus was actually going to be killed, he totally lost it. He was wrecked with guilt and tried to give the thirty silver coins back to the priests. 'I sinned! I betrayed an innocent man!' he cried. They shot back, 'So? That's your problem.' Judas threw the money into the Temple, ran out, and hung himself. So much for blood money.

Jesus stood before Governor Pilate, who asked him, 'Are you the King of the Jews?' Jesus replied with a quiet confidence, 'You said it.' But when the priests and elders started piling on the accusations, Jesus didn't say a word. Pilate was baffled. 'Don't you hear all this stuff they're accusing you of?' he asked. Still, Jesus remained silent. The governor was seriously impressed.

It was a custom to release one prisoner chosen by the crowd during the Passover festival. They had a famous bad guy named Barabbas in jail. Pilate, knowing the religious leaders were just jealous, asked the crowd, 'Who should I release? Barabbas, or Jesus, the so-called Christ?' But the leaders had already hyped up the crowd to demand Barabbas. 'What should I do with Jesus?' Pilate asked. The crowd went wild, screaming, 'Nail him to a cross!' Pilate, confused, yelled, 'But why? What crime has he committed?' But they just screamed louder.

Pilate saw a riot was about to pop off and that he was getting nowhere. He washed his hands in front of everyone and dropped a bomb: 'I'm innocent of this man's blood. This is on you.' The crowd went nuts, shouting, 'We'll take the blame! Us and our kids!' So Pilate freed Barabbas, had Jesus brutally whipped, and handed him over to be crucified.

The governor's soldiers took Jesus into the palace and the whole squad gathered to make fun of him. They stripped him and put a scarlet robe on him, twisted a crown of thorns for his head, and put a staff in his hand like a fake scepter. They knelt down, mocking him, 'Hey, hail King of the Jews!' Then they spit on him and beat him on the head with the staff. When they were done, they put his own clothes back on and led him away to be killed.

On the way out, they forced a random guy from Cyrene, Simon, to carry Jesus' heavy cross. They got to Golgotha, which means 'Skull Hill.' They offered Jesus wine mixed with a painkiller, but after tasting it, he refused. They nailed him to the cross, and then gambled for his clothes. Above his head, they posted the charge: THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS. They crucified two criminals with him, one on his right and one on his left.

People walking by hurled insults, shaking their heads. 'You were gonna destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, right? So save yourself! If you're the Son of God, get down from that cross!' The religious leaders joined in the trash talk: 'He saved others, but he can't save himself! King of Israel, huh? Let's see him come down from the cross, and then we'll believe! He trusted God? Let God rescue him now if he wants him!' Even the criminals crucified next to him dissed him.

From noon until three in the afternoon, the whole land went dark. Around three, Jesus cried out in agony, 'Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?' which means, 'My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?' At that moment, the massive Temple curtain ripped in two from top to bottom. The earth shook, rocks split, and tombs opened. After Jesus rose from the dead, many of God's people who had died were raised to life and appeared to others in the city. The Roman captain and his soldiers who were guarding Jesus were terrified by the earthquake and everything happening. They said, 'Seriously, this man was the Son of God.'

Quite a few women were watching from a distance — women who had followed Jesus all the way from Galilee to take care of Him. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of James and John.

That evening, a rich guy named Joseph from Arimathea showed up. He was secretly a follower of Jesus too. He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus' body, and Pilate gave the green light. Joseph took the body, wrapped it in fresh, clean linen, and laid it in his own brand-new tomb that had been carved out of rock. Then he rolled a massive stone in front of the entrance and left. Mary Magdalene and the other Mary just sat there across from the tomb, watching.

The next day (the day after Preparation Day), the chief priests and Pharisees went to Pilate. 'Sir,' they said, 'we remember that liar said while he was still alive, \u2018After three days I will rise again.\u2019 So order the tomb to be locked down tight until day three. Otherwise his disciples might sneak in, steal the body, and tell everyone he rose from the dead. That last lie would be even worse than the first.' Pilate said, 'Take some guards. Go secure it the best you know how.' So they went, sealed the stone, and posted the guards.

title: He's Back. And It's Everything.
paragraphs: After the Sabbath, at the crack of dawn on Sunday, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to pay their respects at Jesus' tomb. Out of nowhere, the ground started shaking like crazy. A legit angel of God came down from heaven, rolled away the massive stone like it was nothing, and then just sat on it, chilling. The angel was blazing with light, like lightning, and his clothes were whiter than fresh snow. The guards hired to protect the tomb were so freaked out they literally couldn't move. They were basically frozen in fear.

The angel looked at the women and said, "Don't be scared. I know you're looking for Jesus, the one who was crucified. But he's not here. He has risen, just like he said he would. Come on, check out the spot where he was laid." The women peeked inside, and sure enough, the tomb was empty. The angel then gave them their mission: "Now, go quick and tell his disciples that he's risen from the dead and is on his way to Galilee. You'll see him there. That's the message."

The women were a mix of terrified and totally ecstatic. They took off running from the tomb to find the disciples and tell them the insane news. Suddenly, Jesus himself was right there in front of them. "Good morning!" he said. They dropped to their knees, grabbed his feet, and just started worshiping. Jesus told them, "Don't be afraid. Go tell my brothers to head to Galilee. I'll meet them there."

Meanwhile, some of the guards who had fled the scene went into the city and spilled the beans to the high priests about everything that had just gone down. The religious leaders called an emergency meeting and came up with a seriously shady plan. They paid the soldiers a huge amount of money to spread a lie: "Tell everyone his disciples came in the middle of the night and stole his body while we were asleep." They even promised the soldiers they'd have their backs if the governor found out they were sleeping on the job. The soldiers took the cash and did what they were told. And that fake news story is still floating around today.

The eleven disciples booked it to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had told them to meet him. When they saw him, they worshiped him, but some of them were still a little hesitant, not fully sure if they could handle this level of commitment. But Jesus didn't let their doubts slow him down. He came to them and dropped this bombshell:

> "God has given me all authority in heaven and on earth. So go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything I have commanded you. And for sure, I am with you always, to the very end of the age."
